newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh 1997 budget deficit seen at 3.16 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh 1997 budget deficit seen at 3.16 pct of GDP.

text.p: Kazakhstan's 1997 budget deficit will be no higher than 3.16 percent of gross domestic product, a senior economy official told deputies on Monday at the start of a parliamentary session to debate next year's budget.

"There is a temptation to increase the deficit," Daulet Sembayev, head of the upper house of parliament's economics, finance and budget committee, told deputies. "But this sum is the upper limit of a rational budget deficit," he said.
He said the oil-rich former Soviet republic was living beyond its means and was heavily reliant on foreign loans.

He said foreign loans to Kazakhstan would total 43 billion tenge ($567 million) in 1997 while domestic loans would total 11 billion tenge ($150 million) in the same period. The cost of servicing the loans, Sembayev said, would total 17.3 billion tenge ($230 million) or almost 10 percent of the budget.
The government is also under pressure to pay a large backlog of wages and pensions to its 16.9 million people, who are growing impatient with the hardships brought by market reforms.
Sembayev said that as of December 1 this year, the government owed 20.5 billion tenge ($281 million) in wages and a further 7.9 billion tenge ($108.2 million) in pension arrears.
The tenge fell to 73.2312 to the dollar on Monday on the Kazakhstan Currency Exchange from 73.0671 on Friday.
